{{Quote|I think we've got something, sir. The report is only a fragment from a probe droid in the Hoth system, but it's the best lead we've had.''"<br />"''We have thousands of probe droids searching the galaxy. I want proof, not leads!|Captain Piett and Admiral Ozzel|audio=PiettOzzelBestLead-TESB.flac|<ref name="ESB" />}}
A '''Viper probe droid''' served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as part of its search for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance's]] hidden base following their [[Evacuation of Yavin]]. Along with thousands of other [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probes]] of its model, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] was developed for the Empire by [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]] in a project overseen personally by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. Its construction occurred on [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]], a major droid [[Factory/Legends|manufacturing]] planet that, unknown to the Empire or most other organic beings, was under the control of [[IG-88 assassin droid|IG-88]], a quartet of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]]. The IG-88 droids' mastermind, [[IG-88A/Legends|IG-88A]], altered the Viper probe droids' programming so that, even while they carried out the Empire's mission, they also gathered intelligence for a great [[Droid Revolution|droid revolution]] that the assassin was planning.

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyer]] of [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]] launched the probe droid. It flew in its [[Predator I]] [[Hyperdrive pod/Legends|hyperspace pod]] from the [[Ione system|Ione]] to the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]] and crashed down on the frozen surface of the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. The probot emerged from its crash site and began to explore the planet. Before long it located the newly-built [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] and transmitted its data to the command ship ''[[Executor/Legends|Executor]]''. The Rebels soon discovered the probe droid, and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] engaged it in combat. The droid, realizing that it had been discovered, activated its [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destruct mechanism]]. Its mission had already been successful: after seeing its transmitted data, Darth Vader ordered his entire fleet to the Hoth system, launching the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] and the destruction of Echo Base.

==Biography==
===Thousands of Remote Probes===
{{Quote|I sense that something is not right here... but I can't determine what it is. Make certain those probe droids are delivered.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] to Supervisor [[Gurdun]] on Mechis III|<ref name="IG-88" />}}
[[File:Stalker-system-tesb.jpg|thumb|left|A Death Squadron destroyer prepares to launch its probes.]]
The probe droid that would travel to Hoth was one of thousands serving the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. Following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Empire commissioned a new line of Viper probe droids from Arakyd Industries to scour [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] for hidden Rebel bases. In particular, the Empire wished to corner the elusive, mobile [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]],<ref name="GG3" /> while Darth Vader obsessively sought the hiding place of [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="ESB" /> 

Arakyd fulfilled the Imperial order at its droid manufacturing works on [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]]. However, no one in the company, the Empire, nor any other organic being was aware that the IG-88 assassin droids had taken over the works in the [[Mechis III Uprising]]. IG-88A decided to use the new line of Imperial probes to further his long-term goal, a galaxywide [[Droid Revolution]] that would seize power from organic beings. The Viper probots would serve as IG-88's scouts while appearing to serve only the Empire. Even [[Gurdun]], the Imperial supervisor overseeing the Arakyd order, remained unaware that the probots had been co-opted. Darth Vader oversaw the operation from its beginning, personally visiting the droid works; the Sith Lord's visit was the closest the conspiracy ever came to getting discovered. The IG droids masked their purpose so well that Vader only sensed a slight disturbance whose source he could not pinpoint.<ref name="IG-88" />

When the droids' construction was complete, they were delivered to Death Squadron. The Star Destroyers ''[[Avenger/Legends|Avenger]]'' and ''[[Stalker]]'' detached from the Squadron to travel to the [[Ione system]],<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> where they launched probe droids to search the Hoth, [[Allyuen system/Legends|Allyuen]], and [[Tokmia system/Legends|Tokmia systems]], along with other nearby parts of the Galaxy.<ref name="GG3 2nd" /> Just before the destroyer group launched their Viper probes, Vader sent an order that additional commands be added to their programming to prioritize two targets: Luke Skywalker and the starship belonging to Han Solo, the ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]''.<ref name="Freedom's Winter">{{ESBRadio|Freedom's Winter}}</ref>

===Hitting the Ground===
{{Quote|There's a meteorite that hit the ground near here. I want to check it out. It won't take long.|Luke Skywalker to Han Solo|<ref name="ESB" />}}
After launching from its [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] near [[Ione/Legends|Ione]], the Arakyd Viper flew inside its hyperspace pod to the Hoth system.<ref name="Atlas" /> Its reentry rockets fired, bringing it down hard onto the surface of the ice planet of Hoth in a region near the [[North Ridge/Legends|North Ridge]] and [[Lanteel Glacier/Legends|Lanteel Glacier]]. While the probot did not know it yet, it had found the planet where the Rebels were building their new stronghold, Echo Base. Its crash-landing appeared to the casual onlooker, and even the base's sensor readings, as one of many [[Meteorite/Legends|meteorites]] streaking toward Hoth's surface.<ref name="GG3" /> Luke Skywalker and Han Solo were just then riding [[Tauntaun/Legends|tauntauns]] on a routine patrol of the frozen wastes. Skywalker decided to ride alone to inspect the crash site, telling Solo to go on without him.<ref name="ESB" /> Before he could reach the site, Skywalker was attacked by a [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]] ice creature and never saw what had really crashed to the ground. Thus, the Hoth probe droid was free to continue on its programmed mission.<ref name="GG3" /> 

[[File:ProbedroidTCGDesolationofHoth.jpg|thumb|The probot floats across the the desolation of Hoth.]]
The probe droid emerged from its pod and levitated on its [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlifts]] from the still-smoking crater.<ref name="ESBNovel" /> It detected a faint [[Comm unit/Legends|comm]] signal on non-Imperial bandwidths: the signal made by Skywalker's [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] as he spoke with Solo and Echo Base. To the probe droid, this indicated the presence of an unregistered, possibly Rebel, settlement. Since it had not yet gathered enough evidence to report, the droid moved away from the signal to stay hidden and protected until it could learn more.<ref name="GG3" />

The probe droid continued in the direction of the signal's probable destination point. While searching, it encountered what it first took to be an unusually warm mound of ice. The droid understood that this indicated the presence of a creature astoundingly well-adapted to the cold climate.<ref name="ESBNovel" /> Standard scans would not have been able to detect a wampa in this environment,<ref name="Fact File">[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 51|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 51]]</ref> but the probot was equipped with advanced sensor technology beyond the reach of almost anyone but the Empire.<ref name="GG3" /> It fired a probing laser into the mound, awakening and angering the wampa sleeping beneath it. The droid now understood the enraged creature to be a threat; it turned its laser to its maximum intensity and fired, vaporizing it.<ref name="ESBNovel" />

Already the droid had not gone undetected. Solo had placed new [[sentry marker]]s near the crash site, and with them Echo Base was able to pick up the Viper's energy signal, though it was not possible to identify it. The Rebels could not investigate further because a blizzard was beginning to surge throughout the area.<ref name="The Coming Storm">{{ESBRadio|The Coming Storm}}</ref> The same storm made conditions difficult for the probe droid. It settled to the ground and activated its modified power-intensive [[Particle shield/Legends|particle shield]] to protect it from the thick snow. It ceased normal operation, shunting all energy to its shield.<ref name="GG3" /> From the outside, it appeared as nothing but a snow-covered dome.<ref name="ESBNovel" />

===It isn't friendly===
{{Quote|This is Echo Station Three-Eight. Unidentified object is in our scope. It's just over the ridge. We should have visual contact in about&mdash; What the&mdash;? Oh, no!|Station 3-8 trooper just as the probe droid opened fire|<ref name="ESBNovel" />}}
The droid resumed its search when the [[Hoth (star)/Legends|sun]] rose, entering [[Zone Twelve/Legends|Zone Twelve]] outside Echo Base.<ref name="ESB" /> There, it detected the presence of a large [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]]. It began recording this crucial data and transmitting it, via its HoloNet transceiver, to Vader's personal [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']].<ref name="GG3" /> IG-88 on Mechis III simultaneously received the data on a secret channel. He hoped to use it to learn about the Empire's plans and its weaknesses.<ref name="IG-88" /> 

After sending this first report, the probot continued on its mission. It mapped the defenses of Echo Base, including the surrounding trenches, artillery, the [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|anti-orbital ion cannon]], and [[Troop/Legends|troop]] movements and positions. This invaluable, though fragmentary, information would be available to Imperial [[General/Legends|General]] [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]] as he planned his assault on the base.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:EchoStation38destroyed-SW39.png|thumb|left|The probe droid destroys Station 3-8.]]
At this point, the droid was ready to move beyond reconnaissance and begin to sabotage and disrupt Rebel operations; but it was spotted before it could make the attempt.<ref name="GG3" /> A [[Unidentified Rebel trooper (Station 3-8)|Rebel scout trooper]] positioned in [[Echo Station 3-8]] detected a metal object on the far side of a ridge, transmitting something in an unknown code.<ref name="ESBNovel" /> Before the trooper could see the droid or confirm what it was, the probot opened fire and destroyed the outpost with its blaster cannon, reducing it to a smoldering ruin and killing the scout inside.<ref name="Comic 39">[[Star Wars (1977) 39|''Star Wars'' (1977) 39]]</ref>

===Not Much Left===
{{Quote|Princess, we have a visitor. We've picked up something outside the base in Zone Twelve, moving east.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]], to [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="ESB" />}}
As the probe droid continued to transmit its data, Echo Base commander [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] reviewed the findings from Station 3-8. The Rebel [[Translator/Legends|translator]] droid [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], upon hearing the unknown signal, concluded that there was a high probability that it was an Imperial code.<ref name="A Question of Survival">{{ESBRadio|A Question of Survival}}</ref> Han Solo volunteered himself and his [[First Mate/Legends|first mate]] [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] to go on foot to investigate the mysterious machine.<ref name="ESB" /> Rieekan also dispatched [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogues]] [[Rogue Ten/Legends|Ten]] and [[Rogue Eleven/Legends|Eleven]] to patrol the air in [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeders]] at a low altitude and be alert for trouble.<ref name="A Question of Survival" /> The Rogue Flight pilots, [[Tarrin Datch/Legends|Tarrin Datch]] and [[Tenk Lenso]],<ref name="GG3 2nd">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref> brought Solo and Chewbacca to a spot near the droid in Hoth's [[Ceyan Range/Legends|Ceyan Range]].<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref><ref name="ItWoSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

[[File:AbominableChewbacca-SWT.png|thumb|Chewbacca acts as a decoy.]]
Solo reported that the object was a droid and was moving quickly in the direction of the base. Rieekan wanted to order the snowspeeders to attack it, but Solo believed that he and Chewbacca could take care of it more quickly.<ref name="A Question of Survival" /> The probot detected the enemies' approach and began to take evasive maneuvers.<ref name="GG3" /> Chewbacca managed to outflank it and act as a decoy behind a nearby rise. While the probe, distracted, shot at the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]], Han Solo shot it from the other direction. To Solo's surprise, what was meant to be a disabling shot triggered an explosion that destroyed it.<ref name="ESB" /> The probe droid, to protect its sensitive data and programming, set off its self-destruct mechanism.<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:ViperProbeSelfDestruct-TESB.jpg|thumb|left|The probe droid activates its self-destruct sequence.]]
The self-destruct was not entirely effective, due either to the cold or to damage suffered during its landing. Solo and Chewbacca were able to bring part of it back to base, where a team of technicians under [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]] conducted a scan of the intact portions of its memory circuits. Na'al used this data to help compile his subsequent reports on the history of the Rebellion during this period.<ref name="GG3" />

===The Rebels Are There===
{{Quote|The probe droid ceased transmissions very suddenly. We're not sure how, but we think it may have been destroyed.''"<br />"''That is it. The Rebels are there.|Captain Piett and Darth Vader|<ref name="A Question of Survival" />}}
Though the probe droid was destroyed, Imperial [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]] received its scans on the ''Executor'' and believed them to be a promising lead. His superior, [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Ozzel]], was highly skeptical that the fragmented data proved anything, but Vader, through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], was confident that this probe droid had found the sought-after Rebel base.<ref name="ESB" /> He ordered the entire Death Squadron fleet to go to the Hoth System and prepare for a full-scale ground assault.<ref name="GG3" /> Responding to the same signal, [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]], the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] of the IG-88 quartet, left Mechis III for Hoth to observe Vader's actions from a distance.<ref name="IG-88" />

Vader's intuition was correct: the probe droid's intelligence, though incomplete, brought him and his fleet directly to the Rebels' new base. In the battle that followed, General Veers led [[Blizzard Force/Legends|Blizzard Force]] to occupy the base and drive the Alliance from the system. The surviving Rebels scattered across the Galaxy. Both Skywalker and the ''Millennium Falcon'' again slipped past Vader. He continued to pursue them, finally capturing Solo, Chewbacca, C-3PO and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]] and challenging Skywalker to a [[Duel on Cloud City/Legends|lightsaber duel]].<ref name="ESB" /> IG-88B also pursued Solo on Cloud City but was destroyed in a surprise attack by [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].<ref name="IG-88" />

==Characteristics==
Like others of its model, the Viper probe droid sent to Hoth carried out its mission with a mechanical detachment, inquisitive but without emotion.<ref name="ESBNovel" /> Yet it was fully self-aware, carrying the same sentience programming as IG-88 and his would-be partners in the droid revolution.<ref name="IG-88" /> It was singularly focused on its mission to find its target, and a new program ordered by Darth Vader caused it to fixate on any clues leading to Luke Skywalker and Han Solo in particular.<ref name="Freedom's Winter" /> For all that, its ultimate, secret purpose was to gather information to further the cause of the droid revolution. It harbored a sense of respect for IG-88 as the revolution's leader.<ref name="IG-88" />

[[File:ProbeDroid_in_Ceyan_Range_.jpg|thumb|The probe droid was caught by surprise in the Ceyan Range.]]
The probe could approach challenges with flexibility, varying its methods to suit the situation, from stealth, to confrontation, to deadly force.<ref name="ESB" /> This allowed it to evade threats and collect enough data to send back to Death Squadron, which enabled the Empire to find and destroy Echo Base.<ref name="GG3" /> The probot had sufficient firepower and combat skills to defend itself, killing a wampa and making quick work of Echo Station 3-8 before its trooper could relay a full report to base.<ref name="Comic 39" /> Nevertheless, when the droid faced Solo and Chewbacca, it fell for their decoy maneuver and found itself outsmarted. When the time came, the probe droid initiated its self-destruct mechanism without a second thought.<ref name="ESB" /> It knew from the start that its mission might be one of suicide.<ref name="IG-88" />

==Equipment==
The droid was covered in light armor, colored black. It measured 1.6 meters in height and had five manipulator arms extending from a central pod, which worked together with several retractable [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] arms to gather samples.<ref name="GG3" /> One of the arms was high-torque.<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref>  High-resolution receivers and sensors covered its domed head&mdash;including motion, acoustic, sonic, and seismic sensors, a radiation meter, magnetic imager, and [[Holocamera/Legends|holocamera]]. It had an [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] sensor capable of determining a [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] atmosphere class within one half-hour.<ref name="GG3" /> The probot was equipped with a floodlight on its head.<ref name="RS II guide" />

The probe droid relayed information to its superiors via a high-frequency [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] transceiver. When making transmissions, it emitted a audio encrypted imperial code set. It moved on a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] generator equipped to operate over any terrain and move at a speed up to 40 km/h. Like other Vipers, it was delivered to its target planet through a single-use custom built [[Predator I|hyperspace pod]].<ref name="GG3" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-probedroid.jpg|thumb|The probe droid concept art by Ralph McQuarrie.]]
The probe droid in the Hoth system first appeared in the [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]], where several sections are narrated from the droid's point of view. The droid was designed for {{Film|V}}. [[Ralph McQuarrie]] created its concept art, basing it, evidently, on a small robot appearing in a comic by the artist [[wikipedia:Jean Giraud|Moebius]].<ref name="Still Designing">{{InsiderCite|24|Still Designing A Galaxy Far, Far Away: A Profile of "Artiste Extraordinaire" Ralph McQuarrie|Still Designing A Galaxy Far, Far Away: A Profile of 'Artiste Extraordinaire' Ralph McQuarrie}}</ref> 

For ''The Empire Strikes Back'', two models were used to depict the probe droid on film. The first was life-size and was used for the scene in which the droid engages in a firefight against Han and Chewbacca. The model ran on tracks hidden in the snow;<ref name="Making Of">''[[The Making of The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> this together with long shots allowed the crew to make the droid appear to float in the air.<ref name="40th Anniversary Collector's Edition">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back: The 40th Anniversary Special Edition|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'': The 40th Anniversary Special Edition]]</ref> This scene was shot in [[Finse]], Norway on [[March 10]], [[1979]], with [[Harrison Ford]] playing Han and [[Peter Mayhew]] as Chewie. The droid's meteoric landing was accomplished in Finse by a dynamite explosion.<ref name="Making Of" />

[[File:Empire_Probe_BTS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The crew film the large probe droid model in Norway.]]
The second, smaller model was used for the scene in which the probe droid emerges from its crater.<ref name="40th Anniversary Collector's Edition" /> The model was prepared by art director [[Joe Johnston]]. To film the the scene, shot at [[Industrial Light & Magic]], the model was slowly raised through a miniature set representing the snowy surface of Hoth.<ref name="Making Of" /> 

According to [[Ben Burtt]], the film's sound designer, the iconic audio of the droid was actually the electronically-altered voice of "a well-known Shakespearean actor," though he did not identify the performer.<ref name="Skywalker Saga Official Collector's Edition">[[Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga – The Official Collector's Edition|''Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga'' – The Official Collector's Edition]]</ref>

The droid played a major role in the plot of the movie and its adaptations in other media. Nevertheless, it was never given a designation or name within the [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] continuity. In [[Canon]], it first received a designation in the [[2018]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]'', which showed the text "[[XJ9-CS14]]" written in [[Aurebesh]].<ref name="Droidography">''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]''</ref>

===Continuity===
In the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|the radio dramatization of ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] ([[1983]]), dialogue between Captain [[Lorth Needa/Legends|Lorth Needa]] and a subordinate indicates that the Star Destroyer [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']] launched the Viper probe droid that discovered Echo Base.<ref name="Freedom's Winter" /> The [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|Second Edition of ''Galaxy Guide 3'']] ([[1996]]) confirmed this account. However, the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]] (also 1996) gave a contradictory version, introducing the ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]'' as the Star Destroyer that launched the droid. After this, some [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] sources identified the probe droid with the ''Avenger'', others with the ''Stalker''. ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]) harmonizes the accounts by stating that both ships were responsible for deploying probe droids without stating which ship is seen in the film.<ref name="Atlas" />
